intro: Guangzhou rewards visitors with Cantonese food, riverside towers and leafy colonial islands. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Metro: 15+ lines, fares ¥2-21, English signs; tap a foreign contactless card or buy a token.
Yang Cheng Tong stored-value card costs ¥50 (¥18 deposit) and gives 5-40% metro discounts.
Buses are cheap and wide-reaching but slower and harder to read for visitors.
Taxis are metered; ride-hailing apps DiDi and Amap work, Uber does not operate in China.
Driving yourself is not advised for visitors; traffic is heavy and rules differ.
Walking is good in the centre; shared bikes are common for short hops.
Ferries run to Hong Kong and Macau from Nansha and Lianhuashan ports.

canton_tower.name: Canton Tower
canton_tower.price_text: ≈ CNY 150 for the main observation deck; higher decks cost more
canton_tower.hours: Daily roughly 09:30–22:30; check on the day
canton_tower.tip: Go up about an hour before sunset to see the city in daylight and lit up after dark.

chen_clan.name: Chen Clan Ancestral Hall
chen_clan.hours: Daily roughly 09:00–17:00; closed some Mondays, check on the day
chen_clan.tip: Look up at the roof ridges for the ceramic figures, then walk the side courtyards.

pearl_river.name: Pearl River
pearl_river.price_text: ≈ CNY 80–150 for a night cruise; riverside walks are free
pearl_river.hours: Cruises usually evening; riverside paths open all day
pearl_river.tip: A night cruise shows the lit-up towers; a free riverside walk at dusk is nearly as good.

sun_yat_sen_hall.name: Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall
sun_yat_sen_hall.hours: Daily roughly 08:00–18:00; check on the day
sun_yat_sen_hall.tip: The blue-tiled roof is best photographed from the front lawn in the morning.

opera_house.name: Guangzhou Opera House
opera_house.price_text: Free to see outside; show tickets vary
opera_house.hours: Exterior always visible; interior only with a show or tour
opera_house.tip: Come at night when the angular facade is lit; book a performance if you want to go inside.

ctf_finance.name: Guangzhou CTF Finance Centre
ctf_finance.price_text: ≈ CNY 100–200 for the observation deck; check on the day
ctf_finance.hours: Observation deck usually daytime into evening; check on the day
ctf_finance.tip: Clear days only; haze can hide the view from the top.

chimelong.name: Chimelong Paradise
chimelong.price_text: ≈ CNY 200–300 day ticket; check on the day
chimelong.tip: It is far from the centre; allow a full day and check opening hours before you go.

kungfu.name: Kungfu (Kungfu Catering)
kungfu.hours: Daily, usually long hours; check on the day
kungfu.tip: A cheap, fast Cantonese chain for rice dishes and soup; good for a quick lunch.

sysu.name: Sun Yat-sen University
sysu.price_text: Free; campus access may need registration
sysu.hours: Campus grounds daytime; check access rules on the day
sysu.tip: The old south campus has leafy red-brick buildings; carry ID in case of gate checks.

tianhe_stadium.name: Tianhe Stadium
tianhe_stadium.price_text: Free to see outside; event tickets vary
tianhe_stadium.hours: Exterior always visible; inside only for events
tianhe_stadium.tip: Worth a look if you are in Tianhe anyway; check for a match or concert.

qingping_market.name: Qingping Market
qingping_market.price_text: Free to walk; food priced per item
qingping_market.hours: Daily roughly morning to early evening
qingping_market.tip: A busy traditional market for herbs, dried goods and snacks; go early and keep your bag close.

shamian_walk.name: Shamian Island walk
shamian_walk.tip: Quiet tree-lined streets with old colonial buildings; a calm break from the crowds.

dim_sum.name: Cantonese dim sum breakfast
dim_sum.hours: Most restaurants serve dim sum in the morning
dim_sum.tip: Go before 10:00 on a weekday to avoid the queue; order a few dishes at a time.

baiyun.name: Baiyun Mountain viewpoint
baiyun.price_text: ≈ CNY 5 park entry; cable car extra
baiyun.hours: Daily roughly 06:00–21:00; check on the day
baiyun.tip: A green hill with city views; take the cable car up and walk down if it is hot.

beijing_road.name: Beijing Road pedestrian street
beijing_road.price_text: Free to walk; shops priced per item
beijing_road.hours: Shops usually late morning to late evening
beijing_road.tip: Busy shopping street with glass-covered old road remains underfoot; good for an evening stroll.

huacheng_square.name: Huacheng Square
huacheng_square.tip: The big lawn between the towers gives the best free view of Canton Tower at night.

food_street.name: Shangxiajiu food street
food_street.hours: Most stalls and shops daytime into evening
food_street.tip: Old shopping street with snack stalls; try a few small items rather than one big meal.

stays.why: Modern towers, Canton Tower views and the best metro links; good for first-timers.
Big shopping malls, many mid-range hotels and easy metro access to the whole city.
Old-city centre: parks, markets and cheap eats within walking distance.
Quiet tree-lined streets with colonial buildings; a calm base near the river.

food: Start the day with dim sum (yum cha): har gow, siu mai and rice rolls. Go before 10am on weekends or expect a queue.
Try Cantonese roast meats: roast goose, char siu and soy chicken, often sold from small shopfronts at lunch.
Wonton noodles and congee are cheap, filling staples; a bowl is often under ¥30.
Evening dai pai dong and seafood streets are lively; point at what looks fresh and ask the price first.
Drink tea with meals. Tap water is not for drinking; bottled water is cheap everywhere.
more_time: Add a day trip to Foshan for Cantonese martial-arts history and ceramics; trains from Guangzhou South take under an hour.
Ferries run to Hong Kong and Macau from Nansha and Lianhuashan ports; check times and tickets on the day.
Spend a slow morning in Yuexiu Park and the Chen Clan Ancestral Hall if you want more old-city time.
